name: Throttle Down Kustoms Inc.
old_description: We design, engineer, and construct rugged steel front bumpers and rear bumpers for Chevy Silverado, Dodge RAM, Ford F-Series, and GMC Sierra trucks. We also make steel Jeep frames and skid plates. Everything we make is made from CNC laser cut PNO solid steel pate, and hand welded by certified professionals in Moore, Montana, USA. Each truck bumper we offer is better than the factory bumper, and comes with a lifetime warranty.
about:
Throttle Down Kustoms operates from Moore, Montana, where it was established in April 2004 after founder Jeremy Pulse purchased his former employer, Advance Frame Works. Pulse had begun building custom truck bumpers in his spare time during the early 2000s, and growing demand led him to transition to full-time fabrication.

The company designs, engineers, and builds steel front and rear bumpers for Chevrolet Silverado, Dodge Ram, Ford F-Series, and GMC Sierra trucks, as well as steel Jeep frames and skid plates. Production relies on CNC laser-cut PNO steel plate (3/16″ and 1/4″) and CNC mandrel-bent frames using 2″×4″ A500 rectangular tubing, all hand-welded by certified fabricators. A separate line, TreeDogKustoms, produces lightweight aluminum dog boxes for trucks, ATVs, and UTVs. The shop runs a dedicated team of certified fabricators, each trained in chassis fabrication programs.

Customers range from ranch hands and oil-field workers needing heavy-duty bumper upgrades to off-road enthusiasts seeking grille guards, integrated LED lighting, and rock-crawling frames. The company also fulfills custom fabrication requests such as enclosed trailers, street rods, and diesel-powered truggies. Products ship worldwide with a typical lead time of 8 to 12 weeks.

Throttle Down Kustoms emphasizes U.S. manufacturing, a lifetime warranty on every product, and mandrel-bent frames that avoid welded joints for greater strength and precision. Pulse’s WyoTech degree in Auto Body Technology and Chassis Fabrication underpins the engineering approach, and the company hires only graduates of reputable fabrication programs.

name: Thunderbird Molding Elkhart
old_description: Realize cost improvements. Reach your performance potential. Get to market quicker. An experienced resource for high-precision custom plastic injection molding and contract manufacturing, we offer comprehensive mold design, prototyping, engineering, production, and assembly services.
about:
Thunderbird Molding operates from Elkhart, Indiana, with additional facilities in Shelbyville, Illinois, and Greensboro. The company is Thunderbird-owned and actively managed, though its founding year and founders are not publicly disclosed. It began as a resource for high-precision custom plastic injection molding and contract manufacturing.

The company provides comprehensive mold design, prototyping, engineering, production, and assembly services. Its capabilities include custom plastic injection molding, insert molding, over molding via press-to-press transfer, finishing, and secondary operations. With presses ranging up to 1,500 tons and an inventory of more than 800 molds, Thunderbird supports scalable production of parts in the millions as well as economical short-run projects using quick-mold-change systems and proprietary batch molding procedures. It also offers 3D printing for low-volume production using carbon printing technology.

Thunderbird serves medical device manufacturers, defense contractors, automotive OEMs, and producers of drinkware and lighting. The company has helped a medical device manufacturer achieve regulatory compliance and an automaker find solutions with advanced molding processes. Its lens-grade parts, made from contaminant-free polymers, meet critical defense industry specifications.

Thunderbird differentiates itself through repeatable part tolerances of ±0.0002 inches, automated 3D video inspection, and a quality system registered to ISO 9001:2015, ITAR, PPAP, SPI, and UL QMMY2. The company cites a 99% success rate when reworking close-tolerance molds to compensate for shrinkage and warpage, and a 2.5-second cycle time on an 8-cavity mold.

name: Tillet Custom Fabrication
old_description: Welcome to Tillet Custom Fabrication, your trusted and reliable source for all your metal fabrication needs. I provide quality workmanship and exceptional customer service in the Madison, WI area. Contact me today for a free quote.
about:
Tillet Custom Fabrication operates from Middleton, Wisconsin, in the Madison metropolitan area. The business is run by Gabriel, who serves as the primary fabricator and point of contact. No founding year is publicly disclosed, and the ownership structure is not specified beyond the sole-proprietor presentation.

The shop provides a broad range of custom metal fabrication and machining services. Capabilities include CNC plasma cutting, tube bending, welding (including cast iron and exotic metals), and general machining. Work spans marine repairs such as pontoon and skeg restoration, automotive components like custom exhaust systems, turbo kits, roll cages, and brackets, as well as residential and commercial projects including ADA-compliant railings, custom furniture, bistro lighting fixtures, and mailboxes. The shop also produces aerospace-grade vacuum-insulated piping for cryogenic liquids, solar panel frames and mounts, beavertail boat pods, and trailer repairs.

Customers come from marine, automotive, residential, aerospace, solar, and general manufacturing sectors. Examples include boat owners needing pontoon repairs, automotive enthusiasts seeking custom exhaust and turbo components, homeowners and contractors requiring code-compliant railings and custom metal furniture, and aerospace or cryogenic projects requiring specialized piping.

The company emphasizes transparent pricing with upfront estimates, constant communication throughout the project, and free quotes. Gabriel highlights expertise in aluminum, stainless steel, and exotic metals as a core differentiator.

name: Tin Man Duct Fabrication
old_description: Tin Man Sheet Metal Fabrication is a fully automated producer of
about:
Tin Man Duct Fabrication operates from Manassas, Virginia, where it was founded in 2001. The company specializes in sheet metal fabrication, focusing exclusively on ductwork production for the greater Washington, D.C. metropolitan area.

The shop runs fully automated production lines capable of manufacturing SMACNA-compliant ductwork in any quantity, from single fittings to 400,000-pound orders. A computerized pricing system delivers consistent quotes, and a dedicated quality technician inspects and signs every fitting before it leaves the facility. Processes include spiral and flat-oval pipe fabrication, TDC ductwork, welded stainless steel, and fiberglass liner installation, with delivery to job sites across Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, D.C., and eastern West Virginia.

Customers span commercial, residential, industrial, and government sectors. The company does not offer installation, avoiding competition with contractor clients, and instead refers reliable contractors when needed. Its ductwork serves HVAC systems in projects ranging from small residential jobs to large-scale government facilities.

Tin Man differentiates itself by signing every fitting, maintaining a no-compete policy with contractors, and offering fast turnaround including same-day emergency service. The business was built on providing premium ductwork at fair, consistent prices with a focus on reliability and schedule adherence.

name: Tomahawk Manufacturing Inc
old_description: Since 1992, Tomahawk Manufacturing, Inc.®  has been providing the food processing industry with top quality products and services. We thank you for your patronage and look forward to serving you for many more years to come.
about:
Tomahawk Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 1992 in Plymouth, Wisconsin, with a mission to provide the food processing industry an alternative source for spare parts, tooling, and equipment at competitive rates while upholding high standards of ethics and integrity. The company remains privately held and operates today with the same founding vision.

The company designs and builds a line of food forming machines — the TM-26, TM-19, TM-400, and TM-6 — capable of throughputs from 1,200 to 6,000 pounds per hour at up to 100 strokes per minute. In addition to equipment manufacturing, Tomahawk offers customized in-house tooling, spare parts supply, field service, engineering support, and operator training programs. Its operations span a corporate headquarters and manufacturing facility in Plymouth, an engineering office in Hartland, Wisconsin, an automation integration site in Albany, Georgia (Industrial Control Associates), and a European subsidiary in Rijswijk, Netherlands.

Tomahawk serves food processors across beef, poultry, seafood, pork, plant-based protein, pet food, and pet pharmaceutical segments. Its global customer base extends throughout North and South America, Europe, and Asia, supported by a network of regional agents.

The company emphasizes a responsive, customer-first approach, including 24/7 emergency assistance, on-site service, and tooling audits, aiming to minimize downtime and maintain a personal connection with each client.

name: Tomfoolery Wood Co.
old_description: Our Pacific Northwest (PNW) furniture balances mid-century modern restraint with natural warmth, using honest materials, natural wood pallets, and thoughtful details to create heirlooms that feel grounded, calm, and deeply connected to our landscape.
about:
Tomfoolery Wood Co. is based in Kent, Washington, with a workshop in Seattle where it designs and handcrafts solid wood furniture. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but its operation centers on Pacific Northwest craftsmanship.

The shop produces custom furniture including armoires, benches, bookcases, consoles, dressers, vinyl LP storage units, and tables. Each piece is built from responsibly sourced domestic hardwoods — Willamette Valley walnut, white oak, maple, cherry, madrone, and myrtle — selected by hand and finished with custom stain options. Hardware choices include solid brass pulls or wood edge accent pulls, and some compartments feature height-adjustable shelves. Production is done start-to-finish in the company’s own facility, though headcount and floor space are not disclosed.

Tomfoolery serves residential clients and ships nationally; testimonials cite customers in Seattle, Washington; Drury, Missouri; and Portland, Oregon. The company also works with interior design professionals on bespoke commissions, collaborating from concept through delivery.

The company emphasizes sustainability, partnering with regional mills and restoration projects to use salvaged urban and orchard trees, and employs waste-minimizing processes. Its differentiators include a collaborative design process, locally sourced materials with provenance, and a focus on heirloom-quality construction intended to last generations.

name: Tonka Electronics
old_description: ​Tonka Electronics, Inc., was founded on September 1, 1976 as a Manufacturer's Representative and stocking Distributor for the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly industry.  We are a woman owned, small business incorporated in the state of Minnesota.
about:
Tonka Electronics, Inc. was founded on September 1, 1976 in Bloomington, Minnesota, as a manufacturer's representative and stocking distributor for the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly industry. The woman-owned small business was incorporated in Minnesota by founder Mike DeLadi, who established the company on a principle of "No slogans, just service."

The company represents capital equipment lines and supplies the consumables those machines require, including leaded and lead-free solder bar, wire, and paste, fluxes, flux additives, solder masks, and cleaning agents. It operates a fully stocked warehouse and offers services such as "SmartDry" intelligent dry storage for SMT component reels, SMT placement equipment, solder analysis, specialty coating systems, and low-cost resharpening. As a manufacturer's representative, its territory covers Minnesota, North and South Dakota, northwest Wisconsin, and parts of Iowa; as a distributor it ships nationwide.

Tonka serves the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly sector, with additional involvement in the medical industry through fine hard wire cutting tools. Its customers are electronics manufacturers seeking process development support and equipment implementation, and it also sells SpliceRite-branded SMT tape splicing products, cover tape extenders, and carrier tape cutting tools directly via e-commerce.

The founder's motto, "No slogans, just service," underscores a focus on hands-on support rather than marketing. The company describes itself as a "focused" distributor specializing in soldering and cleaning products, and emphasizes close collaboration with customers during new equipment installation and process development.

Topsy Products operates from Oshkosh, Wisconsin, as a custom design and fabrication shop specializing in automotive accessories. The company focuses on developing engineered solutions for off-road vehicles, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

Its product line includes hinge hoist brackets and kits, hoist systems, door storage solutions, radio communications accessories, and general accessories. Each accessory undergoes in-house design engineering and development before fabrication.

Topsy Products serves the automotive aftermarket, targeting off-road enthusiasts and owners of Jeep and Ford Bronco vehicles. Its customer base includes individual consumers purchasing directly through the company’s online store, as well as potential wholesale or retail partners seeking specialized off-road accessories.

name: Toray Plastics (America), Inc.
old_description: At Toray, we carefully design thoughtful materials that surround you; materials that help keep food fresh, provide protection against the sun’s rays, make cars more luxurious to the touch, add value to industrial applications, and much more.
about:
Toray Plastics (America), Inc. operates its headquarters in North Kingstown, Rhode Island, where its Torayfan® and Lumirror® film divisions are based. A second facility in Front Royal, Virginia houses the PEF foam division. The company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Toray Industries, Inc., a Japanese multinational founded in 1926 with over 47,900 employees across 308 subsidiaries worldwide. No founding date for the U.S. entity is disclosed, and the original founders are not named in public materials.

The company manufactures specialty polymer films and foams for converters and manufacturers that produce finished consumer and industrial goods. The Torayfan® division extrudes polypropylene and cast polypropylene films, including metallized OPP and bio-based PET variants. The Lumirror® division produces polyester (PET) films, also offered in metallized and bio-based grades. The PEF division extrudes polyolefin, polypropylene, and polyethylene foams. Together the divisions run multiple extrusion, metallizing, and coating lines, including proprietary LumiLid® extrusion coating systems (XXL5 and TXL5). Facility sizes and annual volumes are not published.

Toray's films and foams serve packaging, label, solar-control window, technical, housing and engineering, and automotive markets. Converters use the materials for food packaging that extends shelf life, for pressure-sensitive labels, for automotive window tinting, and for solar-control glazing in buildings and vehicles. The company cites automotive window tinting and food packaging as specific application examples.

Toray states its corporate philosophy is to contribute to society through the creation of new value with innovative ideas, technologies, and products. The U.S. operation emphasizes environmental sustainability, holding certifications such as ISO 14001, ISCC PLUS, and Rhode Island Green Manufacturing Certification, and frames its manufacturing approach as responsible stewardship for future generations.
